turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. I'll grab your vitals before he comes in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, go ahead. We were stuck on the highway forever, some fender bender by the exit, whole mess.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Mm. Blood pressure is one thirty-two over eighty-four. Pulse 78. Oxygen sat 97 percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. That cuff bites every time. Anyway.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): You're good. He'll be right in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hi. What brings you in?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this cough. Every morning I wake up hacking, and the stuff that comes up is brown. That's the reason I came.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, years. About ten years, maybe longer. It was already going when I was still smoking.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Every single morning, doctor. I hear him from the kitchen, twenty minutes easy.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, she's right. Thick brown phlegm. Not yellow, brown.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Still smoking?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Quit last year. Before that, err, a pack a day, uh, forty years.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He really did quit. I'm still proud of that.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight up or down?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Stable. Hasn't budged.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. I don't really know. I get warm sometimes after lunch, but I never checked it, so maybe that's nothing. Hard to say.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Not prescription ones. I take Mucinex, the gaifenesin, six hundred milligrams, when the phlegm gets bad. Couple times a week.
[SEG0023] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Box is in the bathroom cabinet. He does use it.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, before I forget, our granddaughter Maya had a softball game Saturday. They were down by four, then this little kid, not even ours, hit a triple and the whole place went nuts.
[SEG0025] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She wouldn't take the glove off in the car. Still had dirt on her knees at dinner.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety degrees in those bleachers, we were melting. Got mint chip after, and the coach says next week they play Riverside if the heat breaks. Wild.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sounds fun. Cough worse any time besides the morning?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly just the morning. Rest of the day, err, I'm alright. Garage, errands, all fine.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything help it?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Hot coffee takes the edge off. The Mucinex too, I think. Then it just kind of burns itself out.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me listen. Deep breath. Lungs are clear. No wheeze, no crackles.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Huh. Feels rattly when I first get up though.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not hearing that now. I think this is chronic bronchitis from the smoking years. Working impression, not a locked-in diagnosis.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Chronic bronchitis. My uncle ended up on oxygen down in Florida, different deal, I don't want that road.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm booking spirometry, the breathing test, for this cough. Front desk will put it on the schedule.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the tube you blow in, right?
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. We might do a chest scan if it does not settle after that. Not ordering the scan today.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Should we be scared?
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. I do want him to get a flu shot and the pneumonia vaccine. Pharmacy can do both.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I had a flu shot a couple years back, I think. Pneumonia one, I don't remember that at all.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Get both this season anyway. Come back in three weeks and we'll go over the spirometry.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks, ok. Can I still mow? The yard is a jungle and the neighbor kid wants twenty bucks now.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. Mow the lawn. No restrictions.
[SEG0044] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll stick the vaccines on the fridge calendar so it actually happens.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): She'll nag. She already nags about the trash cans. It's fine.
[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. That's it for today.
[SEG0047] person_1 (NURSE): I can walk you out. Front desk will book that breathing test.

spec.situation: Former smoker who quit last year with a long-standing morning cough and brown phlegm; weight stable; no chest pain; spirometry planned; vaccination advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Dose, frequency, indication, current use supported; brand and generic were spoken as 'Mucinex, gaifenesin,' not exact generic spelling.
bad.text: Mucinex (generic_name=guaifenesin, dose=600 mg, frequency=a couple times a week, indication=phlegm, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient is not taking any prescription medications.
Fever history was uncertain rather than absent: patient said he sometimes gets warm after lunch but has never checked his temperature and was unsure if it was anything.
Cough is mostly limited to the morning; rest of the day he is generally alright.
Hot coffee helps the cough, and Mucinex also seems to help.
Patient reports the chest feels 'rattly' when he first gets up, despite clear exam in clinic.
Doctor explicitly said the chest scan is not being ordered today.
Vaccines can be obtained at the pharmacy.
Patient reported prior vaccination history as uncertain/incomplete: had a flu shot a couple years ago he thinks, and does not remember ever getting the pneumonia vaccine.
